title: Microcost Orchestra — Exportable Journey & Attribution Composer
creator: Marisol Rivera
description: Design and prototype a compact, role-aware composer inside Redwood Console that lets product owners and finance teams build and export token-level cost journeys. Goals: 1) provide an intuitive cost breakdown canvas that ties tokens->routes->models; 2) allow bespoke attribution weights and tag-based rollups; 3) support exportable artifacts (CSV, compressed JSONL, and Parquet) and templated pricing patterns for downstream billing/chargeback. The experience should surface tradeoffs between latency/cost (batching vs direct routing) and show projected unit economics when filters or quantization presets are toggled.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas supports drag-to-group segments and assign attribution percentages per-segment
CSV export with per-token rows + route/model metadata and timestamps
Template manager allows saving 3 pricing presets and applying them to a selected date window
Role-aware view: finance role sees aggregated charge summaries while eng role can inspect raw token traces
Prototype validated in 2 stakeholder reviews with actionable feedback and a follow-up plan
design_decisions: Use a two-pane layout: left is the timeline/composer, right is dynamic breakdown and export panel
Attribution model will default to 'first-prefix' but allow weighted-split and last-touch modes
Export formats: CSV (default), NDJSON (for large exports), Parquet (for analytics teams)
Prefetch summary rows server-side to keep canvas interactive for multi-day ranges
Include lightweight sparklines per-route instead of full flamegraphs to keep screen density manageable

How do we present delta between 'estimated' cost (based on presets) and actual historical cost without confusing users?
Minimum retention window for raw per-token exports given compliance and cost considerations?
